ingredients.item: pork collar or shoulder, sliced 7 mm thick
Steamed rice , lettuce ssam, ssamjang , kimchi , musaengchae spicy radish — the cold, crisp counter this rich cut wants

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Charcoal or cast-iron at medium-high. The slices go on in a single layer; with almost no sugar in the marinade, the grill boss is building crust, not managing lacquer. First side undisturbed 2–3 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the smell is roasted soybean and garlic over browning pork — deeper and darker than any other record at this grill. The underside should be crusty brown and release cleanly.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Flip once, 2 minutes more, pull when the meat's juices bead at the surface and the slice is just firm to a fingertip press. Rest the batch 1 minute; moksal carries a little and finishes gently.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: test piece: crusty edge, juicy interior with a firm-but-tender chew that loin never gives, and the doenjang's savory depth arriving right behind the pork. No sweetness ahead of the meat — if there is, the honey ran heavy.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Scissors into bite pieces, warm platter, straight into ssam with ssamjang or wrapped plain with rice and a strand of musaengchae in the bite.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the ssam test: the crust and the chew are the record's signature — this should taste like the grown-up table at the restaurant, the one that skipped the sweet marinades on purpose.

storageNotes: Marinated slices keep 24 hours. Cooked, 3 days — cold moksal over rice with a fried egg is the intended leftover, the crust softening into the yolk.

Variations: a teaspoon of gochujang stirred into the marinade warms it toward #M11's lane; the same marinade on chicken thighs (#M17's register); leftover marinade simmered 3 minutes into a spoon-sauce for the platter.
